short: RFX proteins recognize the X-box, a pseudo-palindrome built from two GTTRCC-like half-sites separated by zero to three bases. The DNA-binding domain is a 76-residue winged helix that reads bases with its beta-hairpin wing rather than with the usual recognition helix, and two domains bind one X-box cooperatively. Humans have eight members, RFX1-RFX8. RFX1-3 form homodimers and heterodimers and drive ciliary gene programs; RFX5 works in a complex with RFXAP and RFXANK to switch on MHC class II genes; RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and enteroendocrine cells. The full 13-14 bp palindrome is one of the most information-rich motifs in vertebrate collections, which makes RFX hits unusually trustworthy.
long:
## The factors

The human RFX family has eight genes. All share a highly conserved 76-residue DNA-binding domain
(DBD); most also carry dimerization domains (B, C and DIM regions) that RFX1, RFX2 and RFX3 use
to form homodimers and heterodimers with each other. RFX1-3 are the ciliogenic branch and are
broadly expressed, with RFX2 and RFX3 concentrated in tissues that build motile cilia. RFX4 is
largely brain- and testis-restricted and produces isoforms lacking parts of the dimerization
region. RFX5 does not dimerize with other RFX proteins; it functions in the RFX (also called
RFXANK-RFXAP-RFX5) complex that, together with the coactivator CIITA, drives MHC class I and
class II transcription. RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and gut enteroendocrine cells and
works downstream of NEUROG3. RFX7 is broadly expressed and acts downstream of p53. RFX8 is
poorly characterized in humans, and the CIS-BP human RFX8 entry is not a human measurement at
all: it is transferred from a louse (Pediculus humanus) protein at 55% DBD identity.

## The motif

The literature consensus, from the RFX1 crystal structure, is 5'-GTNRCC(N0-3)RGYAAC-3'. In
practice vertebrate RFX models converge on the tighter form GTTGCCATGGCAAC, which is what the
motif data in this family reports (GTTGCCATGG). The two forms are not in conflict: the databases
are dominated by high-affinity selection experiments that pick GTTGCC as the half-site and a
2-3 bp spacer, while the literature consensus is written loosely enough to cover the weaker,
variably spaced sites found in real promoters. The structural explanation is unusual. RFX1 is a
winged-helix (helix-turn-helix) protein, but instead of inserting a recognition helix into the
major groove it uses a beta-hairpin wing to make the base-specific contacts; two DBDs bind
cooperatively on opposite half-sites of a symmetrical X-box. This is why the informative positions
are the GTT/AAC ends and the CC/GG pair inside them, and why the central spacer bases are almost
free. Half-sites alone are real sites: RFX5, RFX6 and RFX7 models in these databases are
essentially single half-sites (GTTGC, GTTGCTA, GTTGCCAGG) with 7-12 bits, whereas RFX1-4 models
reach 20-23 bits. Paralogues within RFX1-4 are not separable by sequence. RFX5 and RFX7 can
sometimes be distinguished from RFX1-3 by the *absence* of a strong second half-site, but that is
an occupancy difference, not a specificity difference.

## Where it acts

X-boxes are promoter-proximal more often than not, typically within a few hundred bases of the
transcription start site of ciliary genes (IFT and BBS genes, dynein subunits, ciliary membrane
proteins) and of MHC class II genes, where the X box sits next to the X2 box and about 15-20 bp
from the Y box. The Y box is a CCAAT element bound by NF-Y, and RFX5 and NF-Y bind the class II
promoter cooperatively; this is the best-characterized composite element containing an X-box. In
motile ciliated epithelium RFX2 and RFX3 co-occupy promoters with FOXJ1, the forkhead factor that
specifies motile cilia, and in Drosophila the equivalent partnership is Rfx with Fd3F. RFX6 in
islets co-occupies enhancers with NEUROD1, PDX1 and NKX2-2. X-box counts are modest for a
vertebrate motif precisely because the full palindrome is long: genome-wide scans typically
recover a few thousand strong matches, most of them at ciliary and immune loci.

## Biology and disease

Loss of the RFX complex causes MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome, complementation
groups C, D and E): RFX5, RFXAP or RFXANK mutations remove X-box binding, class II expression
fails, and patients present with combined immunodeficiency. The original RF-X activity was
defined by its absence in such patients' cells. RFX1-3 are the transcriptional core of
ciliogenesis across animals, and the X-box-driven ciliary program is old enough to predate
metazoans. Rfx3 mutant mice have laterality defects, hydrocephalus and impaired nodal cilia;
combined Rfx1/2/3 loss ablates motile ciliogenesis. RFX6 loss of function causes Mitchell-Riley
syndrome (neonatal diabetes with intestinal atresia); heterozygous truncating RFX6 variants cause
maturity-onset diabetes of the young with reduced penetrance, and Rfx6 is also required to
maintain adult beta-cell identity. RFX7 is recurrently mutated in lymphoid cancers and mediates
part of the p53 response, controlling genes including DDIT4 and PDCD4. An estrogen-receptor-RFX4
fusion has been reported in breast tumors.

## Reading a hit

A full 13-14 bp X-box match is strong evidence, and among vertebrate motifs it is one of the few
where a single high-scoring hit is worth acting on: the palindrome carries about 20 bits, so
chance occurrences in the human genome are rare. What a hit does not tell you is which RFX
protein. RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4 are indistinguishable from sequence, and the practical
question is which of them is expressed in your cell type. Half-site-only matches (GTTGC plus a
purine) are a different matter: at 7-9 bits they occur by chance constantly, and they are the form
in which RFX5, RFX6 and RFX7 models are represented here, so hits on those models deserve much
more skepticism than hits on RFX1-4. Two provenance problems affect this family in CIS-BP: the
RFX8 motif comes from a louse protein at 55% DBD identity and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig at
71%, so neither is a human measurement. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model (evidence code S,
grade B) does not resemble an X-box at all and should not be used.
caveats: Trust full-palindrome X-box hits; treat half-site hits (GTTGC alone) as near-worthless on their own, because they carry under 9 bits. Nothing in the sequence separates RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4, so assign a member from expression, not from the match. The RFX5 model reflects a three-protein complex, not RFX5 alone. In CIS-BP the human RFX8 motif is transferred from a louse protein (55% DBD identity) and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig (71%); neither was measured on the human protein. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model is not X-box-like and looks unreliable.
